messages.subject: Odd localhost behavior
messages.subject_clean: Odd localhost behavior
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

Ever since I updated my mac to OSX 10.9, this weird thing has been happening when working on shiny.  Before, I would edit code, save, then refresh the browser, which would instantly reflect the new code.  Now, however, when I refresh the browser, it gets hung up ... the little refresh circle keeps going and going but never finishes.  The weird solution is to quickly toggle over to the R console, then quickly toggle back to the browser and it finishes refreshing.  I do nothing when I toggle to the console ... just make it the active window for a split second.

Am I the only one?  Any idea what might be causing this?

I'm on Chrome v31.0.1650.63, R v3.0.2, OSX 10.9.

John

messages.subject: Re: shiny-server never release browser's memory.
messages.subject_clean: shiny-server never release browser's memory.
messages.body_plain:
With 02_text when I run it with the Chrome Developer Tools memory profiler, I don't see strong evidence of a memory leak. If you show the Chrome Task Manager and right-click to show the JavaScript memory column, you will see that the "live" memory goes up and down as the garbage collector does its work. I believe the fact that the overall tab memory goes up slowly and then dramatically down once in a while (mine climbed up to 75MB before plunging to 50MB) is also due to the way garbage collection works in Chrome.

Are you sure that your application getting slower and slower is due to memory exhaustion in the browser? That would be quite surprising to me. Do you have a URL we can look at?

Vincent is right. Below is the way I use, e.g. for this app: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/reactive1/

showfiles <-  list(
    aceEditor("server",
              value = paste(readLines("server.R"), collapse="\n"),
              mode="r", theme="cobalt", height="380px",
              readOnly=TRUE),
    aceEditor("ui",
              value = paste(readLines("ui.R"), collapse="\n"),
              mode="r", theme="cobalt", height="270px",
              readOnly=TRUE)
    )

2) Type showfiles where you want in ui.R.

Here are the currently outstanding pull requests (you can see the branch if any highlighted for each pull request):

Showcase mode allows you to easily view an application and it's code at the same time (arranged either above/below or side-by-side) for purposes of illustration and learning. Here's what it looks like:

http://gallery.shinyapps.io/06_tabsets/?showcase=1

If you arrange the app and code side-by-side you'll also notice that reactive evaluation is automatically highlighted in the source view as you interact with the application.

>
> http://spark.rstudio.com/toche/demoCounter/
>
> The main problem is that the app does not "source" the ui.R and server.R. It gives me:
>
> Error: cannot open the connection
>
> I have saved the ui.R and server.R inside a /www/ subfolder, where they can be found at this time, although with some delay and not at every attempt.
>
> Any suggestions?
>
> Another problem I encountered was that I had to rename the app from "demo-counter" to "demoCounter" because it wouldn't accept a hyphen. Other apps I have with hyphens in their name work, e.g. http://spark.rstudio.com/toche/demo-dynamic-matrix
>
>
> Thanks!
>
> Code copied below.
>
>
>
> # https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/IWBghVCcMnI
>
> # ui.R
>
> library("shiny")
>
> shinyUI(
>   basicPage(
>     h4("Shiny App Demo: Reactive Counter")
>     ,
>     tags$hr()
>     ,
>     uiOutput("buttons")
>     ,
>     uiOutput("count")
>     ,
>     tags$hr()
>     ,
>     helpText("Description: A counter starting at 0 and with maximum value 10")
>     ,
>     tags$br()
>     ,
>     checkboxInput("showCode", label="Show shiny source code?", value=FALSE)
>     ,
>     uiOutput("source")
>   )
> )
>
>
>
>
> # server.R
>
> library("shiny")
> library("shinyAce")
>
> shinyServer(
>   function(input, output) {
>
>     sourceFilePath <- "http://spark.rstudio.com/toche/demoCounter/"
>
>     # A reactiveValues object holds the value of the counter
>     values <- reactiveValues(i = 0)
>
>     # Print the value of the counter stored in values$i
>     output$count <- renderUI({
>       h5(paste0("counter = ", values$i))
>     })
>
>     # Show the source code
>     output$source <- renderUI({
>       if (input$showCode) {
>         list(
>           aceEditor("ui"
>           , value = paste(readLines(paste0(sourceFilePath,"ui.R")), collapse="\n")
>           , mode = "r"
>           , theme = "cobalt"
>           , height = "260px"
>           , readOnly = TRUE
>           ),
>           aceEditor("server"
>           , value = paste(readLines(paste0(sourceFilePath,"server.R")), collapse="\n")
>           , mode = "r"
>           , theme = "cobalt"
>           , height = "260px"
>           , readOnly = TRUE)
>         )
>       } else {
>         return(invisible())
>       }
>     })
>
>     # Display buttons in the mainPanel
>     output$buttons <- renderUI({
>       if (values$i == 0) {
>         list(actionButton("increment", "Next"))
>       } else {
>         if (values$i == 10) {# bugs: if you click too fast it will jump to 11, 12, etc.
>           list(actionButton("decrement", "Back"))
>         } else {
>           list(actionButton("decrement", "Back"), actionButton("increment", "Next"))
>         }
>       }
>     })
>
>     # The observers re-run the code whenever the button is clicked
>     # Use isolate to avoid getting stuck in an infinite loop
>     observe({
>       if(is.null(input$increment) || input$increment == 0){return()}
>       values$i <- isolate(values$i) + 1
>     })
>
>     observe({
>       if(is.null(input$decrement) || input$decrement == 0){return()}
>       values$i <- isolate(values$i) - 1
>     })
>
>   }
> )

messages.subject: Re: Load and save default-inputs?
messages.subject_clean: Load and save default-inputs?
messages.body_plain:
On this topic, is it possible to update a fileInput object so that it knows where to look for the previously loaded input file?  I am not sure if it is possible because input$....$datapath seems to point to a temporary directory.  The issue would then be that the user is forced to re-choose the file every time and have priotr knowledge from where the file came from.  Moreover, any other loaded settings would then be overwritten by any observe function calls that are triggered by the upload of the file.

If all else fails, the best solution I can think of is for the GUI to pause and ask the user to upload the file before proceeding with the other update calls.

messages.body_plain:
I started making a web tool for mapping ICD-9 codes to their ICD-10 counterparts and made a db in postgresql.
while using shiny, I am encountering some problems:

1) How to pass the dataobject which has the fetched data from db to the output on the screen.
2) How to pass the user input made in the UI to the condition in query that fetches the data.

I prepared this code but it is not generating any output on screen, please help:

UI.R

library(shiny)

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("ICD-9-10-Mapping"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select a dataset and specify the number
  # of observations to view
  sidebarPanel(
    textInput("icd9", "Type an ICD-9 Code here:",value='3950')),

  # Show a summary of the dataset and an HTML table with the requested
  # number of observations
  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("out"))))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(RPostgreSQL)

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Return the requested dataset
  icd9Input <- reactive({input$icd9})
  #userin <- readLines(file("stdin"),1)
  con <- dbConnect(dbDriver("PostgreSQL"), user="postgres", password="xyz", dbname="ICD_9_10_Mapping", host = "localhost", port = 5432)
  query <- "SELECT icd_10_codes, flags FROM icd_9_10_pro WHERE icd_9_codes='3950'"
  res <- dbSendQuery(con, statement = query)
  out <- fetch(res, n = -1)

  # Generate a summary of the dataset
  output$out <- tableOutput("out")
   icd9 <- icd9Input()
   out(icd9)
})

    )

source('extender.R', local = TRUE)

sourceDirectory('tools/', recursive = TRUE)

ui.R

                   tabPanel("Home",uiOutput("dynButtons"))
))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

shinyServer(function(input,output, session){

    basicItems <- function(x){fluidRow(
        tags$head(tags$style(type="text/css", "select { width: 125px;}")),
        column(1,selectInput(paste0("alpha",x),"",c("table","a","b","c"))),
        column(1,offset=1,selectInput(paste0("beta",x),"",c("variable","1","2","3")))
    )}

    i=1
    items <- basicItems(i)

    output$dynButtons <- renderUI({
        uiOutput("genControls")
    })

        output$genControls <- renderUI({
            fluidPage(
                fluidRow(
                    column(2,offset=10,actionButton("addButton","Add~!"))
                ),
                fluidRow(
                    column(12,getItems())
                )
            )
        })

    addItems <- reactive({
            n_click <- input$addButton

            if(is.null(n_click)) {
                items <- basicItems(i);
                return()}
            if(n_click > 0){
                    i = i+1;
                    items <<- list(items,basicItems(i))
            }
            return()
    })

    getItems <- reactive({
        addItems()
        return(items)
    })

})

I had the same problem. I followed the recommended steps and still had the same result. After much trial and error (I am a rank amateur in Linux), I made Shiny Server work. The problem I was having was that some of the essential R packages needed to make Shiny Server work were out of date. I suggest that you follow the instructions at the link recommended, but add a couple of steps. After installing R, install the R development tools:

sudo apt-get install r-base-dev

Then, update all of your R packages (codetools is particularly critical, I think):

sudo su -  -c "R -e \"update.packages(ask=FALSE,checkBuilt=TRUE,repos='http://watson.nci.nih.gov/cran_mirror/')\""

Next, follow the remaining instructions to install the shiny package as instructed, and the shiny-server. Once I did this, I copied the examples directory '01_hello' into the /srv/shiny-server directory.

After adding these additional steps to the instructions on the Shiny Server website, my instance worked.

I hope this helps.

Hi Vincent,
  Yes, it's possiable and not difficult, just change the 'busy.js' to:

setInterval(function(){
  if ($('html').attr('class')=='shiny-busy') {
    setTimeout(function() {
      if ($('html').attr('class')=='shiny-busy') {
        $('div.busy').show()
      }
    }, 1000)

  } else {
    $('div.busy').hide()
  }
},100)

 Best!

Huidong

messages.subject: Re: reactiveValues in global.R
messages.subject_clean: reactiveValues in global.R
messages.body_plain:
It was designed this way so shiny app users could communicate across time and space. Badly written example here http://spark.rstudio.com/johnharrison/rChat/.

global.R
---------------------
globReact <- reactiveValues(chatDF =
                              data.frame(username = c(''), msgdt = c("A long time ago"), msg = c("Welcome to rChat")
                                         , stringsAsFactors = FALSE))

ui.R
--------------------
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("RChat"),
  sidebarPanel(
    textInput("user", "Preferred Username:", paste0("Luke", sample(1:100, 1)))
    , textInput("msg", "Submit a message")
    , tags$div(actionButton("submit", "Submit", icon("refresh")))
  )
    ,
  mainPanel(
    dataTableOutput("chatLog")
  )
))

server.R
-------------------
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  output$chatLog <- renderDataTable({
    globReact$chatDF
  })

  observe({
    x <- as.numeric(input$submit)
    if(x > 0){
      isolate(globReact$chatDF <- rbind(globReact$chatDF, c(username = input$user, msgdt = as.character(Sys.time()), msg = input$msg)))
    }
    updateTextInput(session, "msg", value = "")
  }
  )

})

messages.subject: Re: The behaviour of "shiny-busy"
messages.subject_clean: The behaviour of "shiny-busy"
messages.body_plain:
Possibly. The problem is that observe() is not formally tied to any specific session (which makes sense, as it's possible to have observers that run outside of any one session). However, I have a couple of ideas to deal with this problem:

1) Provide a formal link between an observer and a session, i.e. observe({...}, session=session). (Or possibly make the link implicit, i.e. we "know" what session you're running in.) This would nicely solve another issue we have, which is that when a session ends, you usually want any observers it created to be suspended.

2) Inside an observer, provide a hint about what related reactives or outputs are going to be invalidated by the side-effects of the observer. This would nicely solve another issue we have, which is that when an observer does lengthy calculations that eventually write reactive values, during the lengthy calculations the outputs that will eventually affected don't have the semi-transparent appearance (which we'll update to make look nicer at some point).

João, the solution David offered should work, except I'd change one thing:

output$cond <- reactive({
   ... return something, probably TRUE/FALSE ...
})
outputOptions(output, "cond", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)

With the bolded command, you do not need the textOutput("cond") in ui.R. But you can refer to output.cond in the conditionalPanel conditions.

Patrick, "value.cond == 0" didn't work for you because "values" is just a reactiveValues variable that you happened to declare in your server.R code--there's nothing special about it that would cause it to automatically be available in the browser side, which is where the conditionalPanel conditions are evaluated. There *is* something special about the input and output variables; both sides know these values. Does that make sense?

messages.body_plain:
There is a very bad SQL injection security flaw in the app as written:

stmt <- paste(query,input$icd9)

Imagine the user types in the textbox "0; DROP TABLE icd_9_10_pro; --", this would cause your database table to be deleted!

Unfortunately there is not a simple solution to this problem at the moment, as the database packages in R seem to be missing the functionality to escape values. I would replace the line above with

stmt <- paste(query, as.numeric(input$icd9))

if the code is meant to be a number. If not, you'll need to bring in the function I have posted here:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/8291758

and call

stmt <- paste(query, sql_quote(input$icd9))

As per the help documentation, I am trying to condition on the "value" arguments of the tabPanels within a navlistPanel call by referring to the navlistPanel "id" argument. For example, if I set id="p1" then I can access the value elsewhere by calling input$p1.

However, the problem I am having is that input$p1 returns NULL always. It does this initially of course. I cannot tell if this is because no tabPanel is initially selected or if it just does not register at all. But it does appear that it only runs once. If I continue to click on the navigation list in the browser, my console does not repeatedly register NULL for input$p1 despite my forced print(input$p1). So it doesn't seem to update.

Interestingly, if I change the function from navlistPanel back to the original tabsetPanel, input$p1 now returns the correct "value" for the active tabPanel and full reactivity is restored. So the argument "id" seems to work for tabsetPanel the same as it always has, but not for navlistPanel, unless I am missing something.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Difficulty passing input values as arguments to function after substitutions
messages.subject_clean: Difficulty passing input values as arguments to function after substitutions
messages.body_plain:
Almost surely I've taken a completely wrong angle on this.

The story is this: Given a function f(a, b), let the user select a or b as the "unknown" x and select a value for the other argument from a slider. For instance, return this f(input$a, "x") and plot f as a function of "x".

My real-world function has several arguments and complicated expressions.

My problem is in "constructing" the function's reactive arguments.

I defined a globalArgs vector in global.R

globalArgs <- c(a = "a", b = "b")

In server.R, I have the following:

    Args <- reactive({
        # 1. copy arguments stored in global.R
        v <- globalArgs
        # 2. replace selected parameter with "x"
        v <- gsubvec(input$X, "x", v)
        # 3. replace all non-selected parameters a with input$a (2 steps!)
        v <- gsubvec(names(globalArgs), lapply(names(globalArgs), function(x) {paste0("ZZZ",x)}), v)
        v <- gsubvec("ZZZ", paste0("input","$"), v)
        # 4. Miracle occurs: input$a as.numeric with "x" as.character or something
        # 5. return a list to use with do.call
        v <- as.list(v)
        return(v)
    })

The problem is that Args() returns "input$a" and "x" with unwanted double-quotes "" around them. There may be other problems too.

You can see from the complicated steps I went through that I'm missing something from the "big picture".

Help is appreciated. The code is below for perusal.

The function gsubvec is in global.R, if you're interested.

library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/anonymous/8297064")
https://gist.github.com/anonymous/8297064

messages.subject: Re: error setting a datatable option that points to a javascript function
messages.subject_clean: error setting a datatable option that points to a javascript function
messages.body_plain:
This is an FAQ about datatables now. The problem is that JSON does not
allow functions (www.json.org <http://www.json.org>), so there is no "official" way of
passing functions from R to JS. Ramnath's workaround is to use a
special character string like "#! function()... !#". I do not know if
we should follow this notion.

You can update the settings of datatables after the initialization,
although the approach is kind of awkward (retrieve the settings,
destroy the table, and re-initialize with new settings):
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/13912363/jquery-datatables-change-rowcallback-after-initialisation

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Yes, it is indeed a huge problem. As I said, the fundamental problem
was from the design of JSON, which just does not allow function
objects. There is basically only one way to go, which is eval(). The
question is how to determine the elements that should be evaluated.
rCharts uses its home-made "#!...!#" notation as a workaround. Another
question is whether eval() can lead to security problems. I have been
thinking for quite a while on this issue, and I guess we will come up
with a solution soon.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Yes, I mean the .swf file, which is not shipped with shiny, and you
have to download it separately: http://datatables.net/download/

After you unzip TableTools-x.x.x.zip, you put the three folders js/,
css/, and swf/ under the www/ directory of your app. Here is a minimal
example:

# ui.R

shinyUI(basicPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$link(href='css/TableTools.css', rel="stylesheet", type="text/css"),
    tags$script(src='js/ZeroClipboard.js'),
    tags$script(src='js/TableTools.js')
  ),
  dataTableOutput('foo')
))

# server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$foo = renderDataTable(
    iris,
    options = list(

      "sDom" = 'T<"clear">lfrtip',
      "oTableTools" = list(

        "sSwfPath" = "swf/copy_csv_xls_pdf.swf"
      ))
  )
})

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: One way to place navlistPanel in sidebar apart from mainPanel content
messages.subject_clean: One way to place navlistPanel in sidebar apart from mainPanel content
messages.body_plain:
Using the navlistPanel function, I found that too much (for my purposes) screen real estate was taken up by having the navigation list show in the main panel area to the right of the sidebar, directly lumped with the tab panels referenced in the navlistPanel() call. So I looked for a way to make it more indirect. I wanted the list to appear as a wellPanel in the sidebar along with my other sidebar inputs.

There may be better ways, but below is what I came up with for anyone who is interested.

One of the benefits of the navigation list is for when there are a lot of elements and a tabsetPanel might appear cluttered. So let's say we have ten tab panels. In my sidebarPanel() call, I include the following:

navlistPanel(
    "Heading 1",
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp1"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp2"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1",value="tp3"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp4"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp5"),
    "Heading 2",
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp6"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp7"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp8"),
    "Heading 3",
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp9"),
    tabPanel("tab panel 1", value="tp10"),
    id="nlp",
    widths=c(12,1)
)

Note that the tab panels above have no content, just a tile and a value. There is nothing to display. This is intended because I only want the list in the sidebar. I want content to appear in the main panel. Also, I could not put zero for the tabset content width, but it allows 12 for the navigation list area even with non-zero content width, which seems to suffice for ensuring that the wellPanel generated is the same full width as any others that occur in my sidebar.

Next, in my mainPanel() call, I just refer to uiOutput("mpContent"), where mpContent is the reactive expression:

mpContent <- reactive({
    x <- NULL
    if(!is.null(input$nlp)){
        id <- input$nlp
        if(id=="tp1"){
            x <- tabPanel("The real tabPanel1",
            #[All content here. divs, plots, tables, text, etc.]
            )
        } else if(id=="tp2") {
            x <- tabPanel("The real tabPanel2",
            #[content]
            )
        ...
        ...
        ...
        } else if(id=="tp10") {
            x <- tabPanel("The real tabPanel10",
            #[content]
            )
        }
    }
    x
})

For all I know, something very similar could be done without the use of navigation lists at all. I only thought to make this kind of design in the sidebar after using the navlistPanel function in the main panel area where it was directly tied to the tabset content being displayed (and realizing it wasn't what I wanted/expected to end up with). So I came to this problem somewhat backwardly. But it looks very nice, and does not seem to introduce any lag or overhead with the extra chain of reactivity involved. Does anyone have any other suggestions for different approaches?

Matt

messages.subject: Apps work with Shiny 0.8.0 but buggy or broken in 0.8.0.99
messages.subject_clean: Apps work with Shiny 0.8.0 but buggy or broken in 0.8.0.99
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I understand version 0.8.0.99 is developmental, but I am curious if I should expect a large number of my previously made apps to no longer function properly when run with this version of Shiny? Several of my apps hosted on Spark for a long time now, and tested and continuing to function perfectly on that server with version 0.8.0, are revealing many bugs and broken functionality when I launch them locally using version 0.8.0.99 (which I've been experimenting with for some of its new features).

It this to be expected? It is a bit troubling, the thought that once the server is upgraded to perhaps version 0.9.0, several apps our clients rely on many no longer work properly. I am searching the best I can for the source of all the bugs, but they seem different from app to app, and difficult for me to pinpoint the sources of the errors. In one case, an app simply did not seem to allow me to name an output reactive for a slider using text that was similar (but not the same) to other variable names. I was able to "fix" the problem in that instance, though I did not understand what was wrong. In other cases I have not found the problems. But in general, it seems to be a pattern of errors showing up in the console (for the sidebar, or for the mainPanel area) that suggest maybe some components on either the user or server side are no longer able to "see" certain objects.

Does anyone have any suggestions on how I can best troubleshoot these problems in a generic way?

Thanks,
Matt

condition = "values.i == 0"

Hi,

That is a good idea, thanks. I was able to find the source of one bug so far by following a breadcrumb trail of print() statements in an app (this tactic probably speaks to my limited debugging Shiny apps).

I just reinstalled 0.8.0.99 and confirmed the issue still exists. I don't know if it counts as a bug or an intended change in behavior. I have reproduced a simple example.

Here is the ui.R

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Title"),
  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("selectionMenu")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    uiOutput("printSelected")
  )
))

And here is the server.R

library(shiny)
mydata <- factor(c("A","B","C"))

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$selectionMenu <- renderUI({ selectInput("selectionMenu", "Choose:", mydata, selected=mydata[1]) })
  output$selected <- reactive({ input$selectionMenu })
  output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") })
})

Up to version 0.8.0, I did not have to do explicit conversion of a factor variable to class character because this happens automatically. Actually, with 0.8.0.99, the value stored in input$selectionMenu still has class character, but it now returns the index of the original factor level instead of the desired value. In this example input$selectionMenu is the character variable "1"," 2", or "3" in 0.8.0.99 whereas it was "A" or "B" or "C" in 0.8.0. It reminds me doing a as.numeric() on a factor without doing as.character() first.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: Apps work with Shiny 0.8.0 but buggy or broken in 0.8.0.99
messages.subject_clean: Apps work with Shiny 0.8.0 but buggy or broken in 0.8.0.99
messages.body_plain:
I have found one more problem that affects sliders in multiple apps when using shiny 0.8.0.99. I do not understand this one though. If I have multiple sliderInput reactives in the sidebar, some display and function properly, while others display as a non-functional (and I think, NULL-valued) textbox that shows the slider's intended default value.

The interesting thing is it seems to be the presence of one slider, that can affect the functionality of another slider (no dependency is intended). Reproducible example below. Note that the first line in sidebarPanel, 'uiOutput("n.trees")', is commented out initially.

ui.R

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Title"),
  sidebarPanel(

#uiOutput("n.trees"),
uiOutput("interaction.depth"),
uiOutput("shrinkage"),
uiOutput("train.fraction"),
uiOutput("bag.fraction"),
uiOutput("cv.folds"),
uiOutput("minobsinnode")

  ),
  mainPanel(
uiOutput("printSelected")
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
output$n.trees <- renderUI({
sliderInput("n.trees","Number of trees:",100,10000,100,step=100)
})

output$bag.fraction <- renderUI({
sliderInput("bag.fraction","Bag fraction:",0.1,1,0.5,step=0.05)
})

output$train.fraction <- renderUI({
sliderInput("train.fraction","Training fraction:",0.1,1,0.5,step=0.05)
})

output$minobsinnode <- renderUI({
sliderInput("minobsinnode","Min. obs. in terminal nodes:",1,10,5,step=1)
})

output$cv.folds <- renderUI({
sliderInput("cv.folds","Cross-validation folds:",1,10,1,step=1)
})

output$shrinkage <- renderUI({
selectInput("shrinkage","Shrinkage rate:",choices=c(0.001,0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1),selected=0.05)
})

output$interaction.depth <- renderUI({
selectInput("interaction.depth","Interaction depth:",choices=1:3,selected=1)
})

output$selected <- reactive({ input$bag.fraction })

output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") })
})

As long as the reactive expression, n.trees, is not included in the sidebar, all the other sliders display and function properly. If you inlcude uiOutput("n.trees") in the ui.R script under Shiny 0.8.0.99, it will display and function properly. However, now most (but not all) of the other sliders will break. The issue seems more nuanced than simply not using periods in reactive names. In fact, I can remove all instances of periods in names in both ui.R and sever.R and it appears this has nothing to do with this particular issue.

I also tried leaving a different output commented out in ui.R in case the issue somehow depended on the number of sliders, but it seems the inclusion of the first slider is the only problematic inclusion. Including it but removing another other one does not remove the problem as removing uiOutput("n.trees") does.

Matt

On Thursday, January 9, 2014 12:34:25 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> I have found one more change, with a simple reproducible example.
>
> I suspect it is not best practice to include a period in a reactive name, at least if one will be using some javascript perhaps? The following works in 0.8.0 but not in 0.8.0.99. It does work again once I remove the period in "dist.type".
>
> ui.R
>
> shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
>   headerPanel("Title"),
>   sidebarPanel(
>     radioButtons("dist.type","Distribution type:",list("Discrete","Continuous"),selected="Discrete")
>   ),
>   mainPanel(
>     uiOutput("printSelected")
>   )
> ))
>
> server.R
>
> library(shiny)
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>   output$selected <- reactive({ input$dist.type })
>   output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") })
> })
>
> At least so far once I find the source, these issues do not appear to be complex problems. It's just the complexity of some of the apps that makes them a bit harder to track down.
> Matt
>
> On Wednesday, January 8, 2014 4:25:39 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I understand version 0.8.0.99 is developmental, but I am curious if I should expect a large number of my previously made apps to no longer function properly when run with this version of Shiny? Several of my apps hosted on Spark for a long time now, and tested and continuing to function perfectly on that server with version 0.8.0, are revealing many bugs and broken functionality when I launch them locally using version 0.8.0.99 (which I've been experimenting with for some of its new features).
> >
> > It this to be expected? It is a bit troubling, the thought that once the server is upgraded to perhaps version 0.9.0, several apps our clients rely on many no longer work properly. I am searching the best I can for the source of all the bugs, but they seem different from app to app, and difficult for me to pinpoint the sources of the errors. In one case, an app simply did not seem to allow me to name an output reactive for a slider using text that was similar (but not the same) to other variable names. I was able to "fix" the problem in that instance, though I did not understand what was wrong. In other cases I have not found the problems. But in general, it seems to be a pattern of errors showing up in the console (for the sidebar, or for the mainPanel area) that suggest maybe some components on either the user or server side are no longer able to "see" certain objects.
> >
> > Does anyone have any suggestions on how I can best troubleshoot these problems in a generic way?
> >
> > Thanks,
> > Matt

messages.body_plain:
I want to ship my ShinyApp as a portable desktop app for Windows. I want to it to be portable so as to minimize friction in take-up. My app is aimed at corporates but they usually have strict software installation policies so normal users can't usually install new software.

I managed to find portable-R and portable-Chrome from portableapps.com <http://portableapps.com>. But if I try to create a batch (.bat) file to fire-up batch mode R which then fires the Shiny-app I will get a black window for the .bat file. What's a nicer way to do this? So that my apps looks a native as possible (even though portable Chrome will popup).

I am also investigating this myself but just wondering if the good people here have any experience doing similar things before (or you all look down on Windows users like me, haha). Hope to write up a tutorial on this to help others once I find a good solution.

messages.subject_clean: Apps work with Shiny 0.8.0 but buggy or broken in 0.8.0.99
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Matthew and Vincent! These are indeed real issues and we are so grateful to you for helping identify them.
The NULL vs. NA issue will be resolved one way or another shortly. My very strong preference is to return the behavior to 0.8.0.
The factors being rendered as numbers is a new bug--we never tested factors as attribute values to my knowledge, and this commit <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/3fc1410> inadvertently changed the behavior. I have filed issue #359 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/359> and pull request #360 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/360> to return the behavior to 0.8.0, along with a unit test.
Dots can be used as the names of variables, but NOT as the names of input or output IDs. Issue #358 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/358> was filed by Winston asking to warn if IDs containing dots are detected. By the way, it's also a bad idea to have an input and output share the same ID (which your n.trees example has, in that each input has the same name as the uiOutput that encloses it). I'm not sure how realistic it is for us to be able to warn in dynamic cases like this though.
The slider and sortable issues are both related to this commit <https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny/commit/92fa1dde798f6a39d8878be4482080cb64fe237c> which was an ambitious attempt to fix a pretty fundamental longstanding bug. The regression it introduces is pretty serious though, I'll work on it tomorrow.
I must apologize for the relatively large number of regressions, we're trying to fix a lot of longstanding issues in 0.9.0 and obviously that kind of ambition increases regression risk. Perhaps we'll do a longer-than-usual beta period for this release. :)

Thanks again!

messages.subject_clean: Apps work with Shiny 0.8.0 but buggy or broken in 0.8.0.99
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Joe!

I always appreciate how fast you all are to address issues that come up. The timely support is so valuable with such a rapidly developing package. It remains a joy to use.

I will adjust my coding style from here forward (and backward, as soon as I can get around to it) to reflect all the coding best practices you suggested.

Once I comb through more of my apps, I will post here again if I find any additional bugs, after freshly re-updating my shiny 0.8.0.99 as Winston suggested in case anything else is fixed in the meantime.

Thanks so much,
Matt

On Friday, January 10, 2014 1:07:48 AM UTC-9, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Thank you Matthew and Vincent! These are indeed real issues and we are so grateful to you for helping identify them.
> The NULL vs. NA issue will be resolved one way or another shortly. My very strong preference is to return the behavior to 0.8.0.
> The factors being rendered as numbers is a new bug--we never tested factors as attribute values to my knowledge, and this commit <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/3fc1410> inadvertently changed the behavior. I have filed issue #359 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/359> and pull request #360 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/360> to return the behavior to 0.8.0, along with a unit test.
> Dots can be used as the names of variables, but NOT as the names of input or output IDs. Issue #358 <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/358> was filed by Winston asking to warn if IDs containing dots are detected. By the way, it's also a bad idea to have an input and output share the same ID (which your n.trees example has, in that each input has the same name as the uiOutput that encloses it). I'm not sure how realistic it is for us to be able to warn in dynamic cases like this though.
> The slider and sortable issues are both related to this commit <https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny/commit/92fa1dde798f6a39d8878be4482080cb64fe237c> which was an ambitious attempt to fix a pretty fundamental longstanding bug. The regression it introduces is pretty serious though, I'll work on it tomorrow.
> I must apologize for the relatively large number of regressions, we're trying to fix a lot of longstanding issues in 0.9.0 and obviously that kind of ambition increases regression risk. Perhaps we'll do a longer-than-usual beta period for this release. :)
>
> Thanks again!
>
>
> On Thu, Jan 9, 2014 at 8:37 PM, Vincent Nijs <vincen...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Not sure if this is related but I have a binding to jquery sortable (http://jqueryui.com/sortable/) that works fine in .80 but no longer works in .8.0.99

> >
> >

> > > I have found one more problem that affects sliders in multiple apps when using shiny 0.8.0.99. I do not understand this one though. If I have multiple sliderInput reactives in the sidebar, some display and function properly, while others display as a non-functional (and I think, NULL-valued) textbox that shows the slider's intended default value.
> > >
> > > The interesting thing is it seems to be the presence of one slider, that can affect the functionality of another slider (no dependency is intended). Reproducible example below. Note that the first line in sidebarPanel, 'uiOutput("n.trees")', is commented out initially.
> > >
> > > ui.R
> > >
> > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
> > >   headerPanel("Title"),
> > >   sidebarPanel(
> > > #uiOutput("n.trees"),
> > > uiOutput("interaction.depth"),
> > > uiOutput("shrinkage"),
> > > uiOutput("train.fraction"),
> > > uiOutput("bag.fraction"),
> > > uiOutput("cv.folds"),
> > > uiOutput("minobsinnode")
> > >   ),
> > >   mainPanel(
> > > uiOutput("printSelected")
> > >   )
> > > ))
> > >
> > >
> > > server.R
> > >
> > > library(shiny)
> > > shinyServer(function(input, output) {
> > > output$n.trees <- renderUI({
> > > sliderInput("n.trees","Number of trees:",100,10000,100,step=100)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$bag.fraction <- renderUI({
> > > sliderInput("bag.fraction","Bag fraction:",0.1,1,0.5,step=0.05)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$train.fraction <- renderUI({
> > > sliderInput("train.fraction","Training fraction:",0.1,1,0.5,step=0.05)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$minobsinnode <- renderUI({
> > > sliderInput("minobsinnode","Min. obs. in terminal nodes:",1,10,5,step=1)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$cv.folds <- renderUI({
> > > sliderInput("cv.folds","Cross-validation folds:",1,10,1,step=1)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$shrinkage <- renderUI({
> > > selectInput("shrinkage","Shrinkage rate:",choices=c(0.001,0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1),selected=0.05)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$interaction.depth <- renderUI({
> > > selectInput("interaction.depth","Interaction depth:",choices=1:3,selected=1)
> > > })
> > >
> > > output$selected <- reactive({ input$bag.fraction })
> > > output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") })
> > > })
> > >
> > > As long as the reactive expression, n.trees, is not included in the sidebar, all the other sliders display and function properly. If you inlcude uiOutput("n.trees") in the ui.R script under Shiny 0.8.0.99, it will display and function properly. However, now most (but not all) of the other sliders will break. The issue seems more nuanced than simply not using periods in reactive names. In fact, I can remove all instances of periods in names in both ui.R and sever.R and it appears this has nothing to do with this particular issue.
> > >
> > > I also tried leaving a different output commented out in ui.R in case the issue somehow depended on the number of sliders, but it seems the inclusion of the first slider is the only problematic inclusion. Including it but removing another other one does not remove the problem as removing uiOutput("n.trees") does.
> > >
> > > Matt
> > >
> > > On Thursday, January 9, 2014 12:34:25 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> > > > I have found one more change, with a simple reproducible example.
> > > >
> > > > I suspect it is not best practice to include a period in a reactive name, at least if one will be using some javascript perhaps? The following works in 0.8.0 but not in 0.8.0.99. It does work again once I remove the period in "dist.type".
> > > >
> > > > ui.R
> > > >
> > > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

> > > >   sidebarPanel(

> > > >   ),

> > > > ))
> > > >
> > > > server.R

> > > > shinyServer(function(input, output) {

> > > >   output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") })
> > > > })
> > > >
> > > > At least so far once I find the source, these issues do not appear to be complex problems. It's just the complexity of some of the apps that makes them a bit harder to track down.
> > > > Matt
> > > >
> > > > On Wednesday, January 8, 2014 4:25:39 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote:
> > > > > Hi,

> > > > > I understand version 0.8.0.99 is developmental, but I am curious if I should expect a large number of my previously made apps to no longer function properly when run with this version of Shiny? Several of my apps hosted on Spark for a long time now, and tested and continuing to function perfectly on that server with version 0.8.0, are revealing many bugs and broken functionality when I launch them locally using version 0.8.0.99 (which I've been experimenting with for some of its new features).
> > > > >
> > > > > It this to be expected? It is a bit troubling, the thought that once the server is upgraded to perhaps version 0.9.0, several apps our clients rely on many no longer work properly. I am searching the best I can for the source of all the bugs, but they seem different from app to app, and difficult for me to pinpoint the sources of the errors. In one case, an app simply did not seem to allow me to name an output reactive for a slider using text that was similar (but not the same) to other variable names. I was able to "fix" the problem in that instance, though I did not understand what was wrong. In other cases I have not found the problems. > > > > > Thanks,

messages.body_plain:
I've found another apparent change in behavior in the browser when using Shiny 0.8.0.99. I have been adding help popovers using your helpPopup() function: https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5913297 A change I am seeing under 0.8.0.99 is that html in the content string is displayed as text. For example, if I enclose text like: '

This is paragraph one.

this is paragraph two.

', this entire string verbatim is what shows up in the popover in the browser, rather than the desired rendering. Matt On Friday, January 10, 2014 9:25:47 AM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote: > Thanks Joe! > > I always appreciate how fast you all are to address issues that come up. The timely support is so valuable with such a rapidly developing package. It remains a joy to use. > > I will adjust my coding style from here forward (and backward, as soon as I can get around to it) to reflect all the coding best practices you suggested. > > Once I comb through more of my apps, I will post here again if I find any additional bugs, after freshly re-updating my shiny 0.8.0.99 as Winston suggested in case anything else is fixed in the meantime. > > Thanks so much, > Matt > > On Friday, January 10, 2014 1:07:48 AM UTC-9, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > > Thank you Matthew and Vincent! These are indeed real issues and we are so grateful to you for helping identify them. > > The NULL vs. NA issue will be resolved one way or another shortly. My very strong preference is to return the behavior to 0.8.0. > > The factors being rendered as numbers is a new bug--we never tested factors as attribute values to my knowledge, and this commit inadvertently changed the behavior. I have filed issue #359 and pull request #360 to return the behavior to 0.8.0, along with a unit test. > > Dots can be used as the names of variables, but NOT as the names of input or output IDs. Issue #358 was filed by Winston asking to warn if IDs containing dots are detected. By the way, it's also a bad idea to have an input and output share the same ID (which your n.trees example has, in that each input has the same name as the uiOutput that encloses it). I'm not sure how realistic it is for us to be able to warn in dynamic cases like this though. > > The slider and sortable issues are both related to this commit which was an ambitious attempt to fix a pretty fundamental longstanding bug. The regression it introduces is pretty serious though, I'll work on it tomorrow. > > I must apologize for the relatively large number of regressions, we're trying to fix a lot of longstanding issues in 0.9.0 and obviously that kind of ambition increases regression risk. Perhaps we'll do a longer-than-usual beta period for this release. :) > > > > Thanks again! > > > > > > On Thu, Jan 9, 2014 at 8:37 PM, Vincent Nijs wrote: > > > Not sure if this is related but I have a binding to jquery sortable (http://jqueryui.com/sortable/) that works fine in .80 but no longer works in .8.0.99 > > > > > > Code here: https://github.com/mostly-harmless/sortable > > > > > > shiny::runGitHub("sortable","mostly-harmless") > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, January 9, 2014 2:28:00 PM UTC-8, Matthew Leonawicz wrote: > > > > I have found one more problem that affects sliders in multiple apps when using shiny 0.8.0.99. I do not understand this one though. If I have multiple sliderInput reactives in the sidebar, some display and function properly, while others display as a non-functional (and I think, NULL-valued) textbox that shows the slider's intended default value. > > > > > > > > The interesting thing is it seems to be the presence of one slider, that can affect the functionality of another slider (no dependency is intended). Reproducible example below. Note that the first line in sidebarPanel, 'uiOutput("n.trees")', is commented out initially. > > > > > > > > ui.R > > > > > > > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( > > > > headerPanel("Title"), > > > > sidebarPanel( > > > > #uiOutput("n.trees"), > > > > uiOutput("interaction.depth"), > > > > uiOutput("shrinkage"), > > > > uiOutput("train.fraction"), > > > > uiOutput("bag.fraction"), > > > > uiOutput("cv.folds"), > > > > uiOutput("minobsinnode") > > > > ), > > > > mainPanel( > > > > uiOutput("printSelected") > > > > ) > > > > )) > > > > > > > > > > > > server.R > > > > > > > > library(shiny) > > > > shinyServer(function(input, output) { > > > > output$n.trees <- renderUI({ > > > > sliderInput("n.trees","Number of trees:",100,10000,100,step=100) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$bag.fraction <- renderUI({ > > > > sliderInput("bag.fraction","Bag fraction:",0.1,1,0.5,step=0.05) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$train.fraction <- renderUI({ > > > > sliderInput("train.fraction","Training fraction:",0.1,1,0.5,step=0.05) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$minobsinnode <- renderUI({ > > > > sliderInput("minobsinnode","Min. obs. in terminal nodes:",1,10,5,step=1) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$cv.folds <- renderUI({ > > > > sliderInput("cv.folds","Cross-validation folds:",1,10,1,step=1) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$shrinkage <- renderUI({ > > > > selectInput("shrinkage","Shrinkage rate:",choices=c(0.001,0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1),selected=0.05) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$interaction.depth <- renderUI({ > > > > selectInput("interaction.depth","Interaction depth:",choices=1:3,selected=1) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > output$selected <- reactive({ input$bag.fraction }) > > > > output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") }) > > > > }) > > > > > > > > As long as the reactive expression, n.trees, is not included in the sidebar, all the other sliders display and function properly. If you inlcude uiOutput("n.trees") in the ui.R script under Shiny 0.8.0.99, it will display and function properly. However, now most (but not all) of the other sliders will break. The issue seems more nuanced than simply not using periods in reactive names. In fact, I can remove all instances of periods in names in both ui.R and sever.R and it appears this has nothing to do with this particular issue. > > > > > > > > I also tried leaving a different output commented out in ui.R in case the issue somehow depended on the number of sliders, but it seems the inclusion of the first slider is the only problematic inclusion. Including it but removing another other one does not remove the problem as removing uiOutput("n.trees") does. > > > > > > > > Matt > > > > > > > > On Thursday, January 9, 2014 12:34:25 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote: > > > > > I have found one more change, with a simple reproducible example. > > > > > > > > > > I suspect it is not best practice to include a period in a reactive name, at least if one will be using some javascript perhaps? The following works in 0.8.0 but not in 0.8.0.99. It does work again once I remove the period in "dist.type". > > > > > > > > > > ui.R > > > > > > > > > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( > > > > > headerPanel("Title"), > > > > > sidebarPanel( > > > > > radioButtons("dist.type","Distribution type:",list("Discrete","Continuous"),selected="Discrete") > > > > > ), > > > > > mainPanel( > > > > > uiOutput("printSelected") > > > > > ) > > > > > )) > > > > > > > > > > server.R > > > > > > > > > > library(shiny) > > > > > shinyServer(function(input, output) { > > > > > output$selected <- reactive({ input$dist.type }) > > > > > output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") }) > > > > > }) > > > > > > > > > > At least so far once I find the source, these issues do not appear to be complex problems. It's just the complexity of some of the apps that makes them a bit harder to track down. > > > > > Matt > > > > > > > > > > On Wednesday, January 8, 2014 4:25:39 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote: > > > > > > Hi, > > > > > > > > > > > > I understand version 0.8.0.99 is developmental, but I am curious if I should expect a large number of my previously made apps to no longer function properly when run with this version of Shiny? Several of my apps hosted on Spark for a long time now, and tested and continuing to function perfectly on that server with version 0.8.0, are revealing many bugs and broken functionality when I launch them locally using version 0.8.0.99 (which I've been experimenting with for some of its new features). > > > > > > > > > > > > It this to be expected? It is a bit troubling, the thought that once the server is upgraded to perhaps version 0.9.0, several apps our clients rely on many no longer work properly. I am searching the best I can for the source of all the bugs, but they seem different from app to app, and difficult for me to pinpoint the sources of the errors. In one case, an app simply did not seem to allow me to name an output reactive for a slider using text that was similar (but not the same) to other variable names. I was able to "fix" the problem in that instance, though I did not understand what was wrong. In other cases I have not found the problems. But in general, it seems to be a pattern of errors showing up in the console (for the sidebar, or for the mainPanel area) that suggest maybe some components on either the user or server side are no longer able to "see" certain objects. > > > > > > > > > > > > Does anyone have any suggestions on how I can best troubleshoot these problems in a generic way? > > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks, > > > > > > Matt > > > > > > -- > > > You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "Shiny - Web Framework for R" group. > > > To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to shiny-discus...@googlegroups.com. > > > For more options, visit https://groups.google.com/groups/opt_out. > >

messages.subject: plotting a function typed in by user - a first demo
messages.subject_clean: plotting a function typed in by user - a first demo
messages.body_plain:
I have made a demo of an app where the user enters a function in  a textInput and a plot is produced. Several properties of the function, such as the ranges and parameter values, may be customized. The plots can also be tweaked to some extent.

https://gist.github.com/ptoche/8376799

This demo app is a by-product of something I was doing for my research, so it's not a full-time endeavour and thus not completely finished and fully tested.

There are many things that I'd like to improve. For instance, right now the user must type in :

function(a=1,b=2,...){a*b}

where only the letters a, b, c, d can be used as functional arguments. I'd like to generalize this to all single letters of the alphabet as well as things like x1, y2, maybe even alpha, beta.

As a priority, I'd like to simplify the input stage, where the user could simply enter:

a*b

in the box, rather than typing out function(etc..

I've only looked at Firefox and Chrome, it's possible that the panels look weird in other browsers. The layout is kind of experimental.

Feedback and suggestions welcome.

You can run the app like this:
library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/ptoche/8376799")

      , "#mainPanelId {min-width: 40%; max-width: 70%;  float: right;}"

  )
}

# ui.R

    mainPanel = wellPanel(
      id = "mainPanelId"
      ,
      # pass customized display settings stored in function gTags() in global.R
      gTags()
      , etc.

Does this work for you?

messages.body_plain:
Hi, I think we have solved both the original problem reported by Basti Hoffmeister and the problem you mentioned (unable to update the `selected` argument only) through https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/340 Please test the development version https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/ Please also note these two items in NEWS: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS * The argument `selected` in checkboxGroupInput(), selectInput(), and radioButtons() refers to the value(s) instead of the name(s) of the argument `choices` now. For example, the value of the `selected` argument in selectInput(..., choices = c('Label 1' = 'x1', 'Label 2' = 'x2'), selected = 'Label 2') must be updated to 'x2', although names/labels will be automatically converted to values internally for backward compatibility. The same change applies to updateCheckboxGroupInput(), updateSelectInput(), and updateRadioButtons() as well. (#340) * Now it is possible to only update the value of a checkbox group, select input, or radio buttons using the `selected` argument without providing the `choices` argument in updateCheckboxGroupInput(), updateSelectInput(), and updateRadioButtons(), respectively. (#340) Regards, Yihui On Thu, Oct 24, 2013 at 9:09 AM, Alex Bokov wrote: > I have just run into this bug as well.   tags$head(
    tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css",
href="styles_black_orange.css"),
    tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="jquery.slider.min.css")
  )

))

Yihui

Hi Alain,

I guess the key is how to retrieve the DataTable object in JavaScript.
You need the option bRetrieve=TRUE, e.g.

runApp(list(
  ui = basicPage(dataTableOutput('foo')),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$foo = renderDataTable(
      iris,
      options = list(bRetrieve=TRUE)
    )
  }
))

Then you can retrieve the table object using:

oTable = $('#foo').find('table').dataTable()

I'm not entirely sure if this will work out, but it can be one
direction that you can go.

Yihui

messages.subject: Re: shiny server occupies terminal
messages.subject_clean: shiny server occupies terminal
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Glad you were able to get the software setup. Running it interactively from a terminal is certainly one option but, as I'm sure you're finding, isn't ideal for a production environment.

Checkout the chapter on starting and stopping Shiny Server <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#stopping-and-starting> in our documentation. The gist is: it's usually preferred to run "always-on" server software like this as a background daemon that starts automatically when your machine boots. I'm not sure what distribution you're using, but you'll likely find that the init.d or Upstart scripts will make this much easier for you.

Depending on which system you're using, starting Shiny Server could be as easy as "sudo start shiny-server" which spawns a background process to run it. Hopefully the docs will explain everything you need to know.

Let us know if you have more trouble!

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yihui,

Thanks so much. This works. At first I thought you might have meant it was simply a matter of load order and I could put these tags at the bottom of sidebarPanel(), in the event I have multiple sliders and don't want to duplicate code. But unless I did it wrong, it does appear that it only loads my slider if I immediately follow the sliderInput call with the css reference.

The other thing I noticed, since I tend to use uiOutput() in conjunction with renderUI() much of the time, is that this only works when sliderInput() is explicitly referenced in ui.R. Fortunately, on t he server side, I was able to achieve the same result with something like the following:

output$Yrs <- renderUI({
if(!is.null(yrs())){
div(
sliderInput("yrs","",yrs()[1],tail(yrs(),1),range(yrs()),step=1,format="#"),
tags$head(tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="jquery.slider.min.css"))
)
}
})

If I have multiple sliders in an app, as well as employing code externalization (with file sourcing) so that for large complex apps not all code is crammed into one or two files, it is not ideal to have this hardcoded in various places. However, at least it works again and does allow me to have a custom slider.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine
messages.subject_clean: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeffrey,

Can you tell from the rpm what version of Shiny Server you have installed? Or could you run this command:

shiny-server --version

I am surprised that you have installation in /srv/shiny-server; the install location should be /opt/shiny-server. My suggestion is that you remove your installation, make sure your file system is clean, and then install the rpm again.

And based on what you said, it seems that you are running on CentOS 5. (You can verify that by running this command: "cat /etc/issue")
If the installation happens correctly, server will start automatically. You can verify that by pointing your browser to http://localhost:3838

And you should be able to use the following command to start (or stop) the server as needed:

sudo /sbin/service shiny-server start

The location of log file is: /var/log/shiny-server.log  please check the file for any errors if your server hasn't started properly.

Hope this helps, and let us if you still have issues.
Fereshteh

messages.body_plain:
I am interested in how you are using ChromPortable. Can you share more on your approach?

I used the command below in a .bat file for my students on windows to start the app. The locale command was needed to get the app to work for those that did not have locale set to English.

C:\PROGRA~1\R\R-30~1.2\bin\x64\R.exe -e "Sys.setlocale(category = 'LC_ALL','English_United States.1252'); shiny::runApp('~/../Desktop/radyant/', port = 8100, launch.browser=TRUE)"

I have something similar for mac using an automator script. Let me know if you are interested.

To stop the app I initially used the following based on Joe Cheng's post at https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/shiny-discuss/close$20r/shiny-discuss/JptpzKxLuvU/boGBwwI3SjIJ

session$onSessionEnded(function() { q("no") })

This stops everything when the user closes the browser window. However it also stops on browser refresh which is a problem for the load/save/reset state functions in my app.

Now I use the following observer in linked to an action button. This shuts down R but it leaves the browser window open.

observe({
  if(is.null(input$quitApp) || input$quitApp == 0) return()
  stopApp()
  q("no")
})

In sum ... no full solution. Hope this still helps a bit.

messages.body_plain:
Fereshteh

Thanks for the reply. I've Solved the problem:

I had installed the library shiny from RStudio but running it as an unprivileged user.
The solution is to run the command:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""  ( http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#install-shiny <http://www.google.com/url?q=http%3A%2F%2Frstudio.github.io%2Fshiny-server%2Flatest%2F%23install-shiny&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNEf4r9uz1Am-vCt7chhK8GXqyMsJQ>)

This command installs the library shiny but as root. After doing this, restart the server shiny-server and now works fine!!

Thanks!!
Pablo

Hi folks  -

I want to do something very similar to the below, as Robert did.  In my case, I want my app to have several control buttons, all in the sidebar of the app,  that are disabled until certain things happen in various tabs of the rest of a multi-tab app.  (I would prefer myself to place the controls of interest IN the tabs they operate with, but I've been requested to keep all controls in the sidebar.  Not my choice!).    I can see from what Joe has written how to go about disabling (greying out, I imagine?) the control buttons, but I am far less clear on how to ENable them at will when I need to do so.  Help?

On Tuesday, January 8, 2013 5:12:24 PM UTC-7, Robert Bruggner wrote:
> Thanks Joe! That worked perfectly - I really appreciate the help.
>
> -Rob
>
> On Jan 8, 2013, at 3:02 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
>
> > OK, interesting.
> >
> > The input controls don't currently support that. Fortunately the HTML generating functions return well-structured lists of tags that are easy to munge. For example:
> >
> > disable <- function(x) {
> >   if (inherits(x, 'shiny.tag')) {
> >     if (x$name %in% c('input', 'select'))
> >       x$attribs$disabled <- 'disabled'
> >     x$children <- disable(x$children)
> >   }
> >   else if (is.list(x) && length(x) > 0) {
> >     for (i in 1:length(x))
> >       x[[i]] <- disable(x[[i]])
> >   }
> >   x
> > }
> >
> > So if you include this function definition at the top of ui.R then you could do e.g.:
> >
> > sidebarPanel(
> >   disable(selectInput(...)),
> >   disable(radioButtons(...))
> > )
> >
> > or whatever.
> >
> >
> > On Tue, Jan 8, 2013 at 2:31 PM, Robert Bruggner <rbru...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > I am generating a multi-paneled UI for an algorithm where in one circumstance, a user may specify algorithm parameters using the actual UI. In another use case, the user provides a config file that is parsed before the UI is launched. Huidong, the problem is that at the time that the inputTracking.js code runs, the controls you want aren't part of the page yet. This is a common problem in jQuery, the solution is to use delegated events <http://api.jquery.com/on/> (scroll down to the section entitled "Direct and delegated events" and read it carefully).

I've created a fork for you that demonstrates this, as well as simplifying the event handling logic:

messages.subject_clean: 'shiny-busy'
messages.body_plain:
Nice one Stéphane.

I'm taking this opportunity to learn too. I think I have discovered good reasons to rely on observe() and isolate() rather than reactive(), though I suppose that mileage will vary depending on the purpose of the app.

I took Stéphane's code and added a few bells and whistles to keep track of what was going on. Namely, I added a numericInput box in which the user can add the delay to be passed to Sys.sleep (totally weird, but it's a demo for learning), and then I attempted to keep track of the total delay when different values of the argument of Sys.sleep were used.

I couldn't get it to work with a simple reactive() like the one you are using. One problem was that Sys.sleep was triggered as soon as the number in the numericInput box was changed and not just when the actionButton was actioned. Another problem was that without isolate-ing various bits of the code, the numbers were all wrong.

I haven't tested extensively, but I think the code below does the calculations right most of the time. If it doesn't, please fix it and get back to me ;-)

I have commented out the code based on a reactive, you can experiment to see what happens to the simple math of keeping track of the delay if you uncomment it.

I use an observe() like so. It is instructive to see what happens if you remove each of the isolate()  and if you remove both, and if you remove the if(is.null(..)){return()}: the math is wrong, each time for different reasons.

 observe({
        input$trigger
        if(is.null(input$trigger) || input$trigger == 0){return()} # needed for math below
        delayValues$total <- isolate(delayValues$total) + isolate(input$delay)
    })

Likewise if you don't wrap your Sys.sleep into an isolate, it will trigger even if the actionButton is not actioned (in this case the math is not updated).

But for your purpose the reactive() approach may well be satisfactory.

https://gist.github.com/ptoche/8461329
library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/ptoche/8461329")

messages.body_plain:
Warning: I'm not an expert or anything.

That I know of: there is a special RStudio way, which is via the rsession.conf file (check the RStudio help pages) and there's a more general way, via the renvironment.site and rprofile.site files (on some systems these files are named .renvironment, etc.) It saves you some typing or saves you from having a special directory call at the top of all your scripts, but be careful because it's only local and it's easy to forget what you have put in those files.

Personally I have a "master file" like this:

# set working directory
if(.Platform$OS.type == "windows"){
  setwd("c:/R/shiny")
} else { setwd("~/R/shiny") }
library("shiny")
runApp("tmp", port=1936)

and I usually have the stuff I'm working on in the tmp directory. I execute the short paragraph above from the RStudio console. That way I also easily remember what I was just working on after I quit.

I use several OS hence the if/windows/else above, you can take it out if you use only one OS.

messages.subject_clean: Cannot configure shiny server on ec2 machine
messages.body_plain:
Solved the problem!  The issue was that the installation needed to run under sudo.  I was logged in as root and just ran a plain command

yum install --nogpgcheck shiny-server-0.4.0.15-x86_64.rpm -y

which gave the error below. The strange issue is that the user 'root' did not show up inside visudo, so it reported that I was not a sudoer and didn't truly complete the install. After I added myself to visudo and reran the install everything worked. Maybe this edge case could be added where if sudo privileges are not available the install should not report Complete!

messages.subject_clean: Improvement ideas
messages.body_plain:
Dmitri,

Until there is an official solution I have an approach to #2 that works. You can try it out if you install the Radiant package at https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant or you can go to http://vnijs.rady.ucsd.edu:3838/marketing/ to see it run on shiny-server

In State in the navbar you can save, load, and reset the state of the app. Basically it saves reactiveValues (values in my app) and the input list. When you load a pervious state it is put into a list called state_list. When inputs are initialized they look for a value in state_list first. If that is not available a general starting value is provided. (most) of the code is available in the file linked below.

https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant/blob/master/inst/marketing/tools/app/state.R

The 4 functions at the top of the file are used to check if an initial value is available. To see how the functions are used in inputs see, for example, https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant/blob/master/inst/marketing/tools/analysis/base.R

On Wednesday, January 15, 2014 10:53:40 AM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Hi Dmitri, thanks so much for the feedback.
>
> #1 is possible already. There's not actually a distinction between input and output "areas" in Shiny, you can put almost any control almost anywhere.
>
> We are working on #2, it's quite easy to do if renderUI is not involved and quite difficult if renderUI is involved!
>
> #3 is coming at some point but in the meantime you could use progressInit/withProgress/setProgress which are available in the shinyIncubator package <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator>. You can install it using devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio") and then use ?shinyIncubator::setProgress to get to the docs. I'll tell you up front, the most common mistake with using these functions is forgetting to include progressInit in your UI. It needs to go somewhere (anywhere, as long as it ends up being part of the page; regardless of where you put it, the progress indicator will end up in the upper right corner of your app).
>
> For #5, the latest builds of Shiny on GitHub master branch allows you to provide datatables callbacks <http://datatables.net/usage/callbacks> as options (the options are passed as an argument to renderDataTables). So something like options=list(fnCreatedRow="function() {...}") should work.
>
>
> On Mon, Dec 16, 2013 at 1:25 PM, Dmitri <dmitr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Improvement ideas:
> >
> > 1) Allow creating control elements in the output area. Sometimes it's very useful. E.g. I run an app to calculate certain metrics on a long list of data (e.g. stocks performance, websites traffic, ads conversion, costs of projects etc.) and have several tabs: most store tables with aggragated metrics, and one stores some charts specific to each element of the dataset (one stock, one website, one ad or certain project). Ideally I would add a dropdown to the tab output area to filter the charts, but now I need to add it to the input area, which is a bit misleading, as it is relevant to one tab only.
> >
> > 2) Make it possible to save the GUI state (state of all dynamic elements and input values) to a string like php.net/serialize <http://php.net/serialize> does. Then it would be possible to efficiently use shiny in tasks like data mining, for example, or any other where you look for ideas using a long list of controls. At the moment every time an interesting setup is found I need to either manually save a long list input values to some Excel file or write a script that goes through all the inputs and writes their values to the database. Same for loading the GUI state.
> >
> > 3) Display "Loading..." or similar message after the actionbutton was pressed, but before the output is displayed. Some of my apps take minutes to run and it's not always clear if the button triggered anything at all before all the calculations finished.
> >
> > 4) DataTables are often filled with numbers and therefore it would be extremely useful to be able to filter individual columns using expressions like ">10" or provide 2 fields one under another for numeric and date columns to set the minimum and maximum values.
> >
> > 5) That's the code I used to catch the event of DataTable being changed to color-code the data. I hope that there is an easier way to do it, but I failed to find one. It would be great to have some identification of the mainPanel update. It was fine when you had all the controls in initial DOM in sidebarPanel, but DataTable is created dynamically and I can't that easily add event listeners to it.

messages.subject: testing a shiny app using testthat?
messages.subject_clean: testing a shiny app using testthat?
messages.body_plain:
As the number of lines of code in my shiny app are increasing I am trying to apply some of the suggestions on testing in Hadley Wickham's Advanced R Programming book/site (http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Testing.html). Specifically, I am trying to figure out if there is way to test (parts of) a shiny app using a script, preferably using testthat.

I have made a (very small) start (see file linked below). The first block works since most of the analyses in my app are done in regular functions. These functions are called from outputs and reactives when the app is run. For testing, however, I am using runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server)) and sink to save output from direct calls to these functions.

https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant/blob/master/inst/tests/test-regression.R

What I would really like to do is call reactives from a script and, depending on the value of input$... , see what output I get. As I wrote in the post linked below, I have an approach to load and save the state of an app that I thought would make testing easy but, unfortunately, I haven't figured out a good way to do it yet.

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/gbLTQPjU0xQ

It would be great to hear how others test their code and if the Shiny/Rstudio folks have suggestions for best practices.

Hi Vincent,

It should be possible to interact with your app using Selenium. I installed radiant from github and had a brief play with it.
I ran radiant using runApp on R process 1. On a seperate R process I ran RSelenium.

# basic script to interact with Radiant
require(RSelenium)
port = 4678
host = "127.0.0.1"
# assume radiant is running
# for simplicity assume a second R is running
# require(radiant)
# require(shiny)
# runApp(system.file("marketing", package="radiant")
#        , host = "0.0.0.0", port = 4678)

# run checkForServer if the standalone selenium server is needed
# RSelenium::checkForServer()

startServer()
remDr <- remoteDriver$new()
Sys.sleep(20) # time for server
remDr$open()
remDr$navigate(paste0("http://", host, ":", port))
# click the navbar button
# necessary as the tab names dont seem to populate untill they are needed
webElem <- remDr$findElement(value = "//*[@class='btn btn-navbar']")
webElem$clickElement()
# get the nav-bar elements
webElem <- remDr$findElements(value = "//*[@class = 'nav']/li/a")
tabTitles <- sapply(webElem, function(x){x$getElementText()})
stateElem <- webElem[[which(tabTitles == 'State')]]

stateElem$clickElement()

messages.subject: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
messages.subject_clean: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to set up a display that is based on two sets of inputs -- call them Option A and Option B.

If I update Option A, I want to regenerate both the data and the appearance components of the display.
If I update Option B, I want to only regenerate the appearance component of the display.

If I just make the display reactive to both input options, then the data is regenerated as well as the appearance components of the display, whenever I change Option B.

So far the way I've solved this is by making the data and appearance components into global variables, so that I can persist the data component outside of the reactive Shiny structure, even when the appearance component is reacting to input changes. But this seems a bad way to fix the problem (I was always taught to avoid global variables wherever possible).

I have an idea that might work: separate Options A and B into different input UI panels, tie the data component of the display to a reactive element, and isolate that element so that it only gets updated when the user presses a Submit button on the Option A panel. But I don't know if that would work (I haven't looked into the Isolate feature in detail yet), or whether it would be the best/cleanest way to do it.

If you have any other suggestions for better ways I could achieve this, I'd love to hear them.

Thanks very much

messages.body_plain:
i think ou can use reactives e.g.

data_for_output <- reactive({
   input$optionA
 ... some code used to generate the data ...
})

output$youroutput <- renderPlot({
  input$optionB
  data <- isolate(data_for_output())
   ....something to generate the output you want...
})

I think you want something like this: optionA now will cause data_for_input() to recompute which in turn will cause output$youroutput to recompute. Chagning optionB doesn't affect data_for_output, but it affects output$youroutput.

      postscript(file, height=6, width=8, onefile = FALSE, horizontal = FALSE)
      print(Plot())
      dev.off()
    })

      print(Plot())

    })

    # Save all answers after click on "submit"

      save(values$A, file = filename, compress = "xz")
    })

messages.subject_clean: changing the color of the headerPanel and marking points on the raster
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shiny community,
I am new in Shiny, and I have a couple question to ask you guys:

First:
How can I change the color of the text in headerPanel ( or wherever text)  in the shinyUI?

Second:
I want plot a raster and I want also mark some points on it.
when I click in a location, the points appears in other location.
Is it about precision?
How can we solver this problem?

The code is:

# ui
shinyUI(basicPage(
  plotOutput("myplot", clickId = "myplot_click", width = 500, height = 500),
  tableOutput("mytable")
))

# server
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  require(raster)
  require(sp)
  r <- raster(xmn=525916.5, xmx=525977.5, ymn=3377900, ymx=3377961, ncols=40, nrows=40)
  r <- setValues(r, 1:ncell(r))

  click_points_data <- data.frame(x = numeric(), y = numeric())

  click_points <- reactive({
    newpoint <- input$myplot_click
    if (!is.null(newpoint))
      click_points_data <<- data.frame(
        x = c(click_points_data$x, newpoint$x),
        y = c(click_points_data$y, newpoint$y))
    click_points_data
  })

  output$myplot <- renderPlot({

    plot(r)
    grid()
    points(click_points()$x, click_points()$y, col = "red")
  })
  output$mytable <- renderTable({
    data.frame(type = rep("click", nrow(click_points())), click_points())
  })
})

I will appreciate any help!
Thank you so much!
Best Regards
ForestCAS
