messages.subject: Re: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
messages.subject_clean: Non-reactive data - best way to set up a display that depends at different times on different inputs
messages.body_plain:
Hi ZJ,

That's really helpful - clarifies things for me.

Unfortunately, after thinking more about the problem, I've realised it's more complicated than I first stated.

The data component of the display only depends on Option A.

The display component depends on Option A and on Option B -- but whenever Option B is updated, I only want to change part of the display component. I want the rest to be perpetuated. If I change Option A, I want the whole of the display component to change.

Basically, I have a list of colours that I want to associate with the different sections of my data. If I choose a new subset of data to display (that's Input A), I want to regenerate the whole set of colours. But I also have a part of the options where the user can change the colour of one section of the data at a time (that's Input B). But I want to perpetuate their choices for the other sections, not regenerate them all.

I guess it might be possible to re-design the input interface so I have conditional input elements, one for every section of the data, that let the user choose the colour for that section of the data.
I know it's possible to have conditional panels, but is it possible to have individual conditional input elements, that are only generated when necessary?

Thanks again

On Tuesday, January 21, 2014 4:03:26 PM UTC+13, ZJ wrote:
> i think ou can use reactives e.g.
>
> data_for_output <- reactive({
>    input$optionA
>  ... some code used to generate the data ...
> })
>
> output$youroutput <- renderPlot({
>   input$optionB
>   data <- isolate(data_for_output())
>    ....something to generate the output you want...
> })
>
> I think you want something like this: optionA now will cause data_for_input() to recompute which in turn will cause output$youroutput to recompute. Chagning optionB doesn't affect data_for_output, but it affects output$youroutput.
>
>
> On Tuesday, January 21, 2014 10:12:55 AM UTC+8, L McMillan wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I want to set up a display that is based on two sets of inputs -- call them Option A and Option B.
> >
> > If I update Option A, I want to regenerate both the data and the appearance components of the display.
> > If I update Option B, I want to only regenerate the appearance component of the display.
> >
> > If I just make the display reactive to both input options, then the data is regenerated as well as the appearance components of the display, whenever I change Option B.
> >
> > So far the way I've solved this is by making the data and appearance components into global variables, so that I can persist the data component outside of the reactive Shiny structure, even when the appearance component is reacting to input changes. But this seems a bad way to fix the problem (I was always taught to avoid global variables wherever possible).
> >
> > I have an idea that might work: separate Options A and B into different input UI panels, tie the data component of the display to a reactive element, and isolate that element so that it only gets updated when the user presses a Submit button on the Option A panel. But I don't know if that would work (I haven't looked into the Isolate feature in detail yet), or whether it would be the best/cleanest way to do it.
> >
> > If you have any other suggestions for better ways I could achieve this, I'd love to hear them.
> >
> > Thanks very much

IE8 and 9 are not supported by Shiny apps, unless they are served using Shiny Server. IE didn't get websocket support until IE10, and Shiny Server provides a workaround to support browsers that don't support websockets.

messages.subject: Asynchronous shiny process
messages.subject_clean: Asynchronous shiny process
messages.body_plain:
I have a shiny app, oiModel,  that analyzes some stock option data.  The data it uses is available daily just after 9AM.  So I want to run a separate shiny process that wakes up every day at roughly 9:05, reads the data (from finance.yahoo.com <http://finance.yahoo.com>) and then saves it to a file.  This file is then used by oiModel whenever the shiny app is run.

So I thought the way to do it would be to have a second shiny app, say updateOptionData that would run asynchronously.     something like this: for the server.
(basically just an endless while loop which executes code then pauses for a day)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
aDayInSec <- 60*60*24
while (T) {
        theTime <- as.POSIXlt(Sys.time(), "EST")
     cat("addSnapShot on:", theTime$mday, "th  at" ,theTime$hour,":", theTime$min,"\n")
     self <- Retained$new(reset=F)
     self$addASnapShot()
        self$saveSS()
        Sys.sleep(aDayInSec)
}
 )

Currently my supervisor's away, and I'd rather not upload the code without first checking with her, but I've attached a screenshot of the UI.

The reference and include populations are the portions of data selected to view.

Below that is a section allowing the user to choose a particular population, and then alter the colour and shape for plotting that population.

I would like the user to be able to change the colours and shapes for all the populations being plotted. Having separate colour & shape dropdowns for every population selected seemed like too much to fit in the input section. Therefore I thought instead I could set up an interface so they could change the colours and shapes of the different populations one after the other.

Input A is the selection of reference and include populations -- if they change that selection then I want to regenerate a set of colours and shapes for plotting the new selection.
Input B is the selection of a new colour and shape for a single population. If they change that, then I only want to change the colour and shape for that population, but leave previous changes for other populations intact.

As an example, the user might pick the first population, "Mahu", and change its colour to green and its shape to "Triangle", and click Update. The plot points for Mahu will change on the graph. If they then select the "Flat" population and change its colour to purple and its shape to "Square", I still want Mahu to stay plotted as green triangles. I do not want Mahu to be reset to the default generated options, which is black and "Plus".

My simple solution has been to change the vectors of colours and shapes to be global variables, that are perpetuated outside of the reactive data and the functions -- but that's not an ideal solution in the long term.

Is that any clearer? Please tell me if the details are still confusing.

Thanks for your help.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to display an SVG image within a Shiny page. It has to be SVG, because it's built using gridSVG, and has JavaScript animation code attached to it.

I've already looked through the code in this Shiny app:

https://github.com/timelyportfolio/shiny-grid-svg

but that's about a year old, and using a deprecated bit of Shiny, namely passing of functions to reactive elements.

My current code looks like this:

ui.R:
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

    headerPanel(title="CatchIT Map", windowTitle="CatchIT Map"),

    sidebarPanel(),

    mainPanel(
        uiOutput("map")
    )
))

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

    output$map <- renderUI(svgHTML("interactiveMap"))

    interactiveMap <- reactive({
        make.map() })
})

where make.map creates an SVG file using the gridSVG package, then outputs all the lines of the SVG file -- these are the final lines of make.map():

    svgoutput <- readLines("rotoiticatches.svg", n=-1)
    svgoutput

The global.R file contains make.map, and the function svgHTML:

svgHTML <- function(outputId)
{
    output <- tags$div(id=outputId, class="shiny-html-output", svg(width="300", height="200"))
}

Unfortunately, when I try to run this Shiny app, nothing happens -- I don't get any error messages, but also the SVG does not appear within the Shiny page.

I also tried using the htmlOutput function within ui.R instead of uiOutput, but that didn't seem to work either.

I've looked through the Shiny documentation for htmlOutput, but I still don't see how it's meant to work, and the example given is too basic to be of any use.

Any suggestions for how I should fix this would be gratefully received.

Thanks very much!

}) > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > output$selected <- reactive({ input$bag.fraction }) > > > > > > > > > output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") }) > > > > > > > > > }) > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > As long as the reactive expression, n.trees, is not included in the sidebar, all the other sliders display and function properly. If you inlcude uiOutput("n.trees") in the ui.R script under Shiny 0.8.0.99, it will display and function properly. However, now most (but not all) of the other sliders will break. The issue seems more nuanced than simply not using periods in reactive names. In fact, I can remove all instances of periods in names in both ui.R and sever.R and it appears this has nothing to do with this particular issue. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I also tried leaving a different output commented out in ui.R in case the issue somehow depended on the number of sliders, but it seems the inclusion of the first slider is the only problematic inclusion. Including it but removing another other one does not remove the problem as removing uiOutput("n.trees") does. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Matt > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Thursday, January 9, 2014 12:34:25 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote: > > > > > > > > > > I have found one more change, with a simple reproducible example. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I suspect it is not best practice to include a period in a reactive name, at least if one will be using some javascript perhaps? The following works in 0.8.0 but not in 0.8.0.99. It does work again once I remove the period in "dist.type". > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > ui.R > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar( > > > > > > > > > > headerPanel("Title"), > > > > > > > > > > sidebarPanel( > > > > > > > > > > radioButtons("dist.type","Distribution type:",list("Discrete","Continuous"),selected="Discrete") > > > > > > > > > > ), > > > > > > > > > > mainPanel( > > > > > > > > > > uiOutput("printSelected") > > > > > > > > > > ) > > > > > > > > > > )) > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > server.R > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > library(shiny) > > > > > > > > > > shinyServer(function(input, output) { > > > > > > > > > > output$selected <- reactive({ input$dist.type }) > > > > > > > > > > output$printSelected <- renderUI({ verbatimTextOutput("selected") }) > > > > > > > > > > }) > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > At least so far once I find the source, these issues do not appear to be complex problems. It's just the complexity of some of the apps that makes them a bit harder to track down. > > > > > > > > > > Matt > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > On Wednesday, January 8, 2014 4:25:39 PM UTC-9, Matthew Leonawicz wrote: > > > > > > > > > > > Hi, > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > I understand version 0.8.0.99 is developmental, but I am curious if I should expect a large number of my previously made apps to no longer function properly when run with this version of Shiny? Several of my apps hosted on Spark for a long time now, and tested and continuing to function perfectly on that server with version 0.8.0, are revealing many bugs and broken functionality when I launch them locally using version 0.8.0.99 (which I've been experimenting with for some of its new features). > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > It this to be expected? It is a bit troubling, the thought that once the server is upgraded to perhaps version 0.9.0, several apps our clients rely on many no longer work properly. I am searching the best I can for the source of all the bugs, but they seem different from app to app, and difficult for me to pinpoint the sources of the errors. In one case, an app simply did not seem to allow me to name an output reactive for a slider using text that was similar (but not the same) to other variable names. I was able to "fix" the problem in that instance, though I did not understand what was wrong. In other cases I have not found the problems. But in general, it seems to be a pattern of errors showing up in the console (for the sidebar, or for the mainPanel area) that suggest maybe some components on either the user or server side are no longer able to "see" certain objects. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Does anyone have any suggestions on how I can best troubleshoot these problems in a generic way? > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks, > > > > > > > > > > > Matt > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > -- > > > > > > > > You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "Shiny - Web Framework for R" group. > > > > > > > > To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to shiny-discus...@googlegroups.com. > > > > > > > > For more options, visit https://groups.google.com/groups/opt_out. > > > > > > >

I think that the main difference (Joe correct me if I'm wrong) is that
the navbarPage creates all of the UI as tab panels and then just shows
and hides them as the user navigates. I haven't looked at the
implementation closely but it appears to me as if Joe's bindings don't
create any tabs but rather use dynamic UI rendering from the server.

The former approach allows navbarPage to work the same as other tab
panels (e.g. supports updateTabsetPanel, eventually support
bookmarking, etc.) so is in general preferable. Joe, is there a way we
could make isHidden less expensive and/or is there any other
straightforward way out of this box you can think of?

J.J.

messages.subject: Re: Is there any better way to stop a Shiny app besides Ctrl+C
messages.subject_clean: Is there any better way to stop a Shiny app besides Ctrl+C
messages.body_plain:
To stop the app from within Shiny I initially used the following based on Joe Cheng's post at https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!searchin/shiny-discuss/close$20r/shiny-discuss/JptpzKxLuvU/boGBwwI3SjIJ

session$onSessionEnded(function() { q("no") })

This stops R when the user closes the browser window. However it also stops on browser refresh which can be a problem.

Now I use the following observer linked to an action button (as Jeff also suggests). This shuts down R but it leaves the browser window open.

observe({
  if(is.null(input$quitApp) || input$quitApp == 0) return()
  stopApp()
  q("no")
})

Oops. Wrap any reference to session$vals in an isolate({}) chunk in that last observer. Otherwise that observer will take a dependency on session$vals. Otherwise it will continually update itself.

But hopefully the general idea comes through. I think this would be a scalable solution for you whether you're running it locally like you are now or even if you wanted to deploy this on Shiny Server someday.

Jeff

Hello,

I've encountered a very puzzling behavior when using DataTables (the javascript ones).

I have a data frame with numeric data where numeric columns are converted to characters with decimal separator, using format(round(x, 0), big.mark = ","). The resulting data frame is than feed to renderDataTable.

I'm receiving different results when sorting such columns in browser: on Mac and Windows, they are sorted properly (in increasing numerical orders), while on Linux (CentOs 5.9), they are sorted alphabetically . I made sure that R environments are exactly the same - same R version, same shiny library version (0.8.0), etc.

We cannot use DataTable's sorting plugins[1] at the moment[2], it seems. renderDataTable has somewhat cryptic message in it's documentation string - "Paging, searching, filtering, and sorting can be done on the R side using Shiny as the server infrastructure". I'm not sure what exactly should I do to sort my numeric columns properly on the server side?

Any help on how to sort numeric columns with decimal separators properly would be much appreciated!

Victor

[1] http://datatables.net/plug-ins/sorting
[2] https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/QHYDqEK217U/do4CfRN0uEsJ

Yup; you got it. Sorry the documentation didn't make it clear, but you can use app_dir to host an application at a particular URL. If you use an app_dir inside:

location / {
  app_dir /srv/...;
}

Then you'll be hosting a single application at the base URL.

Jeff

messages.subject: Secure password handling
messages.subject_clean: Secure password handling
messages.body_plain:
I have developed a first prototype for handling passwords in a secure way, and would like to ask anybody with interest in the topic to provide some feedback to it. I put it into the gist at https://gist.github.com/ojessen/8656652

The beef is in the following function:

> # I'm following the recommendations in
> # https://crackstation.net/hashing-security.htm
> salt = paste0(runif(1, max = 1e9),runif(1, max = 1e9))
> hash = digest(paste0(salt,input$loginRegister), algo="sha256")
> # userTable as standin for the table in the database.
> # The aim is to avoid having to
> # login_clear obviously is for testing the behaviour,
> # and not supposed to be in a real app.
> if(!exists("userTable", envir=.GlobalEnv)){
> userTable <<- data.frame(user = input$userNameRegister,
> login =hash,
> login_clear = input$loginRegister,
> nacl = salt)

Looks neat!  You could also consider using rscrypt <https://github.com/rstudio/rscrypt> which provides scrypt hashing instead of just sha256 and may simplify some of your logic with maintaining a separate salt.

messages.subject: File download issues with Shiny Server behind an Apache Reverse Proxy
messages.subject_clean: File download issues with Shiny Server behind an Apache Reverse Proxy
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we're running the Open Source edition of Shiny Server behind an Apache Reverse Proxy and we cannot seem to get file downloads (using Shiny's downloadHandler() function) working.

This is our Apache configuration:

<Location /dashboard>
  ProxyPass http://localhost:3838/dashboard
  ProxyPassReverse  http://localhost:3838/dashboard
</Location>

The Shiny app "dashboard" is running smoothly, no problems here, but whenever we try downloading a file, all we get is a text file containing the temp file name of the download. The file gets correctly created in /tmp/RtmpSA9lN2/file2de0487d470a (or whatever :-) ), but instead of serving up this file, Apache serves a file containing only this filename as text content.

Here's a curl output of what happens:

$ curl -v 'https://[removed]/dashboard/session/[removed]/download/downloadReport?w='
[SSL stuff removed]
> GET /dashboard/session/[removed]/download/downloadReport?w= HTTP/1.1
> User-Agent: curl/7.24.0 (x86_64-apple-darwin12.0) libcurl/7.24.0 OpenSSL/0.9.8y zlib/1.2.5
> Host: [removed]
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Date: Mon, 28 Oct 2013 14:09:31 GMT
< content-disposition: attachment; filename="My_Report.html"
< cache-control: no-cache
< x-ua-compatible: chrome=1
< content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
< content-length: 32
<
* Connection #0 to host [removed] left intact
/tmp/RtmpSA9lN2/file2de0487d470a* Closing connection #0

This is the code used in server.R for specifying the downloadHandler:

  output$downloadReport <- downloadHandler('lc_report.html',
                                           content = function(file) {
                                             file.copy('report/lc_report.html',
                                                       file)
                                           },
                                           'text/html')

Downloads work perfectly fine when the app is executed locally via runApp().

Has anyone encountered a solution/workaround for this issue?

Thanks!

Alex

.shiny-progress {
  position: absolute;
  width: 35%;
  top: 30%;
  right: 20%;
  padding: 12px;
  border: 1px solid #CCC;
  border-radius: 8px;
  background-color: #f5f5f5;
  opacity: 0.9;
}

This works for me, but I'm wondering if I just misunderstood the .js code, or missed some other option for positioning?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
messages.subject_clean: Shiny apps with choroplethr package
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm a big fan of shiny apps.  The dialect map that was covered in business week last year was a lot of fun to play with.

I just released a package for facilitating choropleth maps in R called choroplethr (https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr).  One of the early users of my package tried to create a shiny app using choroplethr.  In theory this would be great because then you would have an interactive map of arbitrary census data on a webpage.  He claims that he can run it locally, but that when he uploads it to rstudio's hosting service it does not work.  His issue report is here: https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr/issues/1.

I am not sure why this would be the case, but there seem to be 2 possible culprits.

1.  He claims that glimmer (is that the name of RStudio's shiny hosting service?) is using R 2.15.  Is this correct?  There seem to be some known issues with choroplethr and R 2.15.  I am about to put an explicit R version requirement because of this.  But I am not sure why glimmer would be using an old version of R.  See https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/choroplethr/Owv7NgAacGE for a discussion of the issues with version 2.15 and choroplethr.

2.  Using the census features of choroplethr requires setting an census api key with the acs.R package's api.key.install function.  I don't know how the transfer of code and state work in the upload process from a local machine to rstudio's hosting service.  Is there an init() function somewhere where the api key can be set?  Is this code publicly available (i.e. can anyone see his api key?).

My user's shiny app is here: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/pssguy/acs/

Is there any way that I can help debug it remotely?

Thanks.

Ari

messages.subject: Segmenting the server.r
messages.subject_clean: Segmenting the server.r
messages.body_plain:
Greetings all,

I have several concurrent apps which are mostly derivative upon one earlier prototype, and have since diverged, but many down stream portions remain the same.  Upon submission of my first completed app yesterday, today I thought it would be worth passing the updates from the down stream portions to the other apps- but that became tedious rather quickly.  So instead, I have been looking for a way to segment the server.r into modules which can be updated and applied to all apps with one file being copy/pasted, rather than going through and finding which changes were made and applying them manually.

I first tried simply putting the modules into .R files, and loading them via source(), but of course this was naive and failed.  I recalled seeing someone else do something similar, so I pulled it up.
server.r*
source("server_01.R")
source("server_02.R")

server <- function(input, output) {
  server_01(input, output)
  server_02(input, output)
}

shinyServer(server)
*
server_01.R and server_02.R were organized as*
server_02 <- function(input, output) {
  .power_gui <- 2
#normal server.r looking stuff
}
*
This seemed promising, however, the two servers did not attempt to share reactives between each other, as when I tried using this approach, the errors "function not found" popped up.  I tried including the reactives in with (input, output, reactive(), reactive2(), etc()) in the initializing functions, but the result was a different error for the unexpected (.  So my last attempt was to use the session variable, (input,output,session), but this too failed.

The next thing I was going to test was making a list object containing every single reactive, that was used in the subsequent portions, and passing that to the servers (input, output, listObject), but I wanted to ask if anyone had a better solution to this?

And as a last note, completely unrelated, I was thinking about the etymology of the name "shiny", the best I can figure is that the devs are a fan of the show Firefly, where the word shiny was used as a synonym for "cool" or a generally good thing.  Though many other television shows use the word shiny as something of interest for their dumb characters, such as Homer Simpson or The Tick.  Can you tell it's a Friday?

Thanks for your time and attention,
Mike
